# LiFePO4 is the better choice for most people

LiFePO4 (also called LFP) lasts several times longer and fails less violently. NMC's only real advantage is lower weight, and in finished power stations that advantage is small. Most major brands have already switched to LiFePO4.

## How they compare

| | LiFePO4 (LFP) | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Rated cycle life** | Typically 3,000–6,000. The median in one 54-model database is 4,000. | Typically 500–1,000. The median in the same database is 800. |
| **Weight** | A little heavier | Lighter. The cells are much denser, but whole stations are only about 10–16% lighter per Wh. |
| **Failure behavior** | Cooler and slower. In one test it smoked without flames. | NMC cells threw flames and ignited in the same test. |
| **Price** | Now mainstream and often cheaper per Wh | Mostly older or ultra-compact models |

Sources: [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/).

## Does it matter for how you'll use it?

- **Daily cycling (van, RV, off-grid, daily solar):** Choose LiFePO4. A 500-cycle NMC unit wears out in about 1.4 years at one cycle a day. A 3,000-cycle LFP unit lasts about 8 years. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))
- **Occasional outage backup or a few trips a year:** Either chemistry works. The battery will age with time before it runs out of cycles, so storing it as the manual says matters more. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))
- **Weight is critical:** Compare the specific models rather than assuming NMC is lighter. The LFP Anker SOLIX C1000 stores more Wh per pound than the NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

## Common myths

- **"LiFePO4 is fireproof" or "it handles overcharge better."** Neither is true. In a 2020 study, the LFP cell reached thermal runaway earlier under overcharge. It was simply milder once it failed. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))
- **"LiFePO4 is better in the cold."** Mostly not. Most stations of either chemistry won't charge below 32°F. Check the manual for the model you're considering. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))
- **Comparing cycle numbers directly.** Check what each rating is measured to. "4,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "4,000 cycles to 80%."
